sentences.text: To address blood-related side effects from previous PARP inhibitors that blocked both PARP1 and PARP2 enzymes, researchers designed a study to identify new drugs specifically targeting PARP1 for brain tumor treatment.
Using Caco-2 cell tests to assess barrier crossing, the team found that compound 33 stopped and shrank tumors in animal models when administered at a dose of 0.2 mg per kilogram once daily.
Computer models suggested that humans would require less than 150 mg of the drug once daily to achieve effectiveness, according to the authors' conclusion based on these computational predictions.
